originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news item: The Indian stock market has been losing value for five days in a row, mainly because oil prices are high and foreign investors are taking their money out. Even though the market recovered a bit during the day, overall sentiment is still weak due to rising interest rates in the US and uncertainty around the world. This means that investors are feeling cautious and unsure about what to do. Analysts are watching certain levels in the Nifty index to see what might happen next, and they're also looking at how individual stocks are performing. The market's ability to bounce back will be important to watch on Monday.

originalTitle: US Fed action, oil swings to test bullion as traders eye West Asia risks: Analysts
simplifiedContent: This is an important week for gold and silver prices. The US Federal Reserve is about to decide whether to change interest rates, and this decision will affect the prices of gold and silver. At the same time, changes in oil prices and tensions between the US and Iran are also being watched closely, as they could also impact gold and silver prices. These factors, along with some key economic announcements, will all play a role in determining what happens to gold and silver prices. This means that investors should pay close attention to the news this week to see how these events might affect their investments.

originalTitle: GS, Nomura, Axis hired to run Carlyle’s India automotive platform IPO
simplifiedContent: Carlyle, a private investment company, is planning to sell part of its ownership in an Indian auto-parts company called Highway Roop Precision Technologies through a process called an Initial Public Offering (IPO). The IPO is expected to raise $500 million and could value the company at $2 billion. Carlyle has hired several banks, including GS, Nomura, and Axis, to help manage the sale. This matters because it's a way for Carlyle to make money from its investment in the company. The sale is mostly about existing owners, like Carlyle, selling their shares, rather than the company itself raising new funds.

originalTitle: Kiwi Will Outpace Euro on Widening Rate Gap, Strategists Say
simplifiedContent: Some experts think the New Zealand dollar (also called the Kiwi) will get stronger compared to the European euro. This is because they believe the central bank of New Zealand will raise interest rates more quickly than the central bank of Europe. As a result, the Kiwi is expected to reach its highest value against the euro in over a year. This matters because it can affect investments and currency exchange rates. The experts' prediction is based on the idea that higher interest rates in New Zealand will make its currency more attractive.

originalTitle: Wall Street Week Ahead: Fed decision, big tech earnings and Middle East conflict in focus
simplifiedContent: This week, investors are waiting to hear from the Federal Reserve, which is expected to keep interest rates the same. This means that the cost of borrowing money will likely stay between 3.50% and 3.75%. The Federal Reserve's decision is important because it can affect the overall economy and the stock market. Investors are also watching for news from big technology companies, which will be releasing their earnings reports, and monitoring the situation in the Middle East for any potential impact on the market. These events may cause some changes in the stock market, so investors are paying close attention.

originalTitle: CBDT issues crypto asset reporting guidelines for exchanges under Income-tax Act 2025
simplifiedContent: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has created rules for cryptocurrency exchanges to report information under the Income-tax Act 2025. This means that companies that buy and sell cryptocurrencies will have to follow these guidelines. The rules are part of a larger framework for reporting cryptocurrency transactions, which has been supported by the G20, a group of major countries. This is important because it will help countries share information about tax payments related to cryptocurrencies. The new guidelines aim to improve international standards for sharing tax information, which can help prevent tax evasion.
